data.narrative: The student demonstrated exceptional discipline in scoping and defining vertical slices, successfully translating ambiguous marketplace requirements into actionable, progressive increments. They showed strong resilience against stakeholder scope creep by proposing a pragmatic, risk-isolated payment spike instead of compromising their MVP architecture.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified the core risk of the marketplace (demand-side booking validation) and structured the MVP to test exactly that.
dimension_scores.evidence: Chose Option B (Demand-first with ultra_thin scope).

dimension_scores.observation: Structured slices progressively, ensuring infrastructure (like the DB schema in Slice 1) supported subsequent layers (Slice 2 supply integration).
Explicitly recognized payment integration as a high-risk external dependency and isolated it.
dimension_scores.evidence: Pushed back against the PM to keep Stripe out of the core booking flow demo.

dimension_scores.observation: Produced highly specific anti-scope definitions that act as protective contracts against feature creep.
dimension_scores.evidence: Anti-scope for Slice 1 explicitly banned auth, payments, emails, and provider registration.

dimension_scores.observation: Responded to unexpected investor pressure with a pragmatic, documented solution rather than blind capitulation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Drafted a dual-demo strategy in artifacts/pm-response-module-04.md (Slice 1 Core + Slice 1.5 Spike).

dimension_scores.observation: Planned the convergence of hardcoded demand flow (Slice 1) with dynamic supply registration (Slice 2).
dimension_scores.evidence: Slice 2 acceptance criteria requires the homepage to read dynamically from DB instead of hardcoded seeds.

data.recommendation: Carry this precise anti-scope discipline into Module 5 Task Specification to ensure AI agents do not hallucinate out-of-scope features.

public_evidence.student_action: Defined 4 progressive vertical slices for a marketplace MVP with strict anti-scope, and drafted a professional response to reject stakeholder scope creep.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Isolated a high-risk Stripe integration into a standalone 'Payment Spike' to protect the delivery of the core booking flow demo.
public_evidence.proof: artifacts/slices-module-04.md containing explicit Acceptance Criteria and Anti-Scope for Slice 1.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Proves the candidate can translate ambiguous requirements into tight engineering scope, and defend that scope professionally against external pressure without derailing the project.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Authored 4 progressive slices that deliver end-to-end user value rather than horizontal technical layers.
Explicitly documented features NOT being built to manage stakeholder expectations.

teaching_approaches.detail: Used the investor payment request to simulate real-world scope negotiation.
